notes:
Lead profile: early-stage devtool startup building a code assistant and in-editor helpers. Inbound came from organic blog post about long-context embeddings + GitHub integration. They want hosted API (self-serve) to move fast but will sign a small paid commitment if pricing and rate limits fit.

Product/technical needs (from calls):
- Primary workload: code assistant and contextual search across large monorepos. Sessions can include 100k+ tokens of extracted context (file snippets + dependency graphs).
- Key asks: low-latency interactive completions (target <200ms token latency for local edits), high concurrency for beta (200-500 concurrent users), bursty traffic (build-time indexing + live editing), and long context support (prefer models that accept >32k tokens or chaining with embeddings).
- Rate limits: want flexible per-account rate-limit policies; ask for burst windows and per-key TPS ceilings. Concerned about 429s during peak internal hack nights.
- SDKs: need official Node and Python SDKs with easy streaming/WebSocket examples; also asked if we have a lightweight Golang client or Retrofit-style REST examples for their backend workers.
- Streaming & function-calling: want example for token-level streaming with source-map metadata (filename + line ranges) and guidance on how to attach provenance for generated edits.
- Cost sensitivity: very price-aware — asked for quantized model options or recommended smaller context/per-token tuning to reduce costs while keeping dev experience snappy.
- Security/compliance: currently just SOC2 in plan; require SSO/SAML for team; audit logs are a must for later enterprise customers. Data residency not a blocker today (US ok).

Commercial/tactical notes:
- They signed up self-serve and used free credits to run initial tests; express interest in moving to a small paid monthly plan if POC shows stable latency.
- Cited competitors: openai gt/gpt endpoints and Anthropic for safety controls; they prefer Redwood if we can provide clearer cost predictability and simpler SDKs.
- Quote from CTO: "We need something that's predictable during peak dev hours — latency spikes break the flow for engineers." — used in notes to emphasize SLOs.

Next actions & asks from AE/SE:
- Provide a 2-scenario pricing estimate: (a) beta: ~300 concurrent users, 10M tokens/mo; (b) scale: 2k concurrent, 50M tokens/mo. Include quantized model options.
- Share Node + Python streaming sample repos (small snippets showing function-calling + provenance headers).
- Confirm rate-limit primitives and how to request temporary burst increases during launches.
- Offer 1x 2-week extension of free credits for a short POC if they commit to a paid trial.

Blockers:
- Legal/Security needs timeline for SSO/SAML and audit log retention (they may pause commitment until SAML is supported),
- Unclear exact concurrency profile (asked for telemetry sample format — SE to send template),
- Budget: founder wants ARR estimate before procurement discussion.

Stipulated links: pricing/deck and security FAQ on Drive above. Jira RDW-1187 created to track sample telemetry ingestion and rate-limit documentation.
